purpose: A small, high-quality adversarial matrix (quality over count) combining two or more stressors per case, executed against real, unmodified production code (real Postgres where DB-backed).

cases.name: structural corruption + amendment DELETION
cases.finding: A corrupted node targeted by a real DELETE_TEXT effect is still correctly withheld (OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL, currentText null) -- deletion semantics (which normally produce a clean RESOLVED null-text outcome per Phase 3F.1.4 P3) never bypass the structural-health gate.

cases.name: duplicate SECTION label + definition lookup
cases.finding: A genuinely duplicate SECTION label (AMBIGUOUS under resolveUniqueNodeByRef) coexisting in the same document as an unrelated, unique definition never contaminates that definition's lookup -- getDefinition resolves the correct, single, real occurrence regardless of the unrelated structural ambiguity elsewhere in the document.

cases.name: sibling claim + review event
cases.finding: Two sibling MaterialSemanticUnits under the same parent SECTION (6.03(a)/(b)), both UNREPRESENTED, produce two independently persisted ClaimReviewItem rows with distinct claimKeys and distinct sourceEvidence -- no cross-contamination despite the shared parent.

cases.name: same defined term, two different documents/instruments
cases.finding: 'Permitted Liens' defined identically (same term, same sectionRef label '1.01(pl)') in two unrelated documents resolves independently per document at every layer checked (index.getDefinition, semanticUnitId, persisted ClaimReviewItem.documentId) -- zero cross-instrument leakage.

cases.name: superseded node + source trace
cases.finding: getNodeSupersessionStatus correctly reports KNOWN_SUPERSEDED (with full provenance: effectId, amendment document) for a real displaced node, and fails closed to UNKNOWN_SUPERSESSION_STATUS (never CURRENT_OPERATIVE) for any document never covered by the supplied operative-state computation.

cases.name: concurrent ingestion + cross-tenant collision attempt
cases.finding: Two DIFFERENT companies uploading byte-identical content SIMULTANEOUSLY (Promise.all, real Postgres) never dedupe against each other -- each gets its own real Document row, distinct artifactIds, and neither company's Document is reachable through the other's companyId-scoped query. This is a genuinely new combined scenario, not covered by the existing tests/connectors/upload-connector.test.ts concurrency suite (which only exercises SAME-tenant concurrency).

cases.name: unsupported semantic expression + review lifecycle
cases.finding: An UNREPRESENTED claim's persisted ClaimReviewItem survives a full lifecycle: CREATED -> ACCEPT (RESOLVED_ACCEPTED) -> re-detection on a later pipeline run -> REOPEN (back to OPEN_REVIEW) -- with a complete, append-only ClaimReviewDecision trail (ACCEPT then REOPEN, never overwritten) and a growing ClaimReviewObservation history. Confirms invariant #37's 'a resolved claim re-detected as still-unresolved reopens, never silently stays resolved' guarantee end-to-end against real Postgres.

cases.name: verification contradiction + amendment supersession
cases.finding: A provision with BOTH an unverified/uncompiled unit AND a later real supersession is reported via STALE_SUPERSEDED_TEXT_CREDITED, correctly OVERRIDING reconciliation's own independent (and different) verdict (UNREPRESENTED, since nothing was ever compiled/discovered for it) with OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED and supersession-specific reasoning. Confirmed the two concepts are never conflated: reconciliation's pre-override reasoning never mentions supersession, and the final, authoritative reasoning explicitly names it.

summary: 8 of 8 constructed adversarial cases passed against real, unmodified production code -- no NEW defect was found beyond the one already isolated and reported in Section 27 (Chain 2's DEFINITION-kind ambiguity gap, which this matrix's Case 2 deliberately did not re-target since it is already fully diagnosed there). Case 6 in particular is a genuinely new adversarial combination (cross-tenant concurrency) not covered by any pre-existing test in this repository.
